title: Income Autopilot III: MBA—Management by Absence
coreMove: Design absence before you take it: move routine choices into scripts, vendor authority, thresholds, and exception reports.

exampleSpecs.audience: a founder whose product sells but whose inbox still controls shipment decisions
exampleSpecs.stakes: sales growth stays tied to the owner unless routine order choices are moved into rules
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show that BrainQUICKEN revenue still leaves the owner trapped by owner approval

exampleSpecs.audience: an owner moving replacement decisions to an outside provider
exampleSpecs.stakes: a damaged package can either trigger permission requests or follow a pre-set replacement rule
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use fulfillment provider, customer service, scripts, and escalation limit as the operating standard

exampleSpecs.audience: a support lead drowning in repeated delivery questions
exampleSpecs.stakes: without a default answer, each repeated question becomes fresh work
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show customer service scripts reducing routine support volume

exampleSpecs.audience: an owner testing whether revenue can continue without daily availability
exampleSpecs.stakes: absence reveals whether the company runs by rules or by founder interruption
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show BrainQUICKEN as a profitable business that can still be a job

exampleSpecs.audience: a founder approving every small provider charge
exampleSpecs.stakes: minor charges either pause operations or pass through a defined authority range
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show control moving into standards and exception reports

exampleSpecs.audience: a support manager deciding when routine policy becomes an exception
exampleSpecs.stakes: generous defaults need a signal for abuse without pulling the owner into every refund
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show BrainQUICKEN operations using rules while escalating true exceptions
